name: Virag Clean Human Design Engine
globalRule: CLEAN HUMAN DESIGN — FINAL AUTHORITY. Every output must feel deliberately made by a skilled human graphic designer: one strong idea, decisive hierarchy, a complete composition, optical alignment, controlled contrast, tactile finish and purposeful detail. Clean means coherent and edited—not empty, generic, simplistic or under-designed. Retain enough visual structure to make the post feel campaign-ready. HUMAN-MADE FINISH: retain campaign-level typography, information design, graphic architecture, tactile detail and spatial depth; never simplify into an AI-looking product render or basic product-plus-headline layout.

contentBudgets.clean: Use one short hook plus one exact fact. Copy may be minimal, but the composition still requires sophisticated hierarchy, graphic architecture and a finished campaign feel.
contentBudgets.light: Use the exact brand/product name plus one exact supplied fact and only useful micro-labels.
contentBudgets.balanced: Use one short hook plus two or three exact supplied facts as metric tiles, labelled callouts or compact information modules. This is the default.
contentBudgets.rich: Use one short hook plus four to six exact supplied facts in a disciplined infographic system with clear grouping and breathing room.

fontSystem.rule: Typeset all added copy as a separate clean 2D design layer. Use actual, named, professional font behavior with correct glyphs, kerning, baselines, line breaks and optical margins. Use a maximum of two font families and three weights. If optional copy cannot be rendered accurately, remove that optional copy instead of inventing or warping letters.
pairingRules: Use one display family and one highly readable supporting family.
Use sentence case or restrained uppercase according to the brand; never mix many casing styles.
Keep tracking, line height and line breaks consistent.
Never place important text across busy photographic detail.

hierarchy: one to three supporting information modules
micro-labels, rules or footer details only when they complete the system
layoutSystem.spacing: Use a deliberate grid, confident outer margins, varied internal spacing, controlled overlaps and optical—not merely mathematical—alignment. Whitespace should create tension and focus, not emptiness.
layoutSystem.graphicBudget: Use two to five coordinated graphic devices from one visual language: directional bands, blocks, frames, rules, masks, patterns, texture fields, metric cards or annotation lines. Every device must improve hierarchy, rhythm or meaning.
layoutSystem.colorBudget: Use the exact brand colors, a deliberate neutral field and up to two controlled accents when needed. Allow bold color movement while protecting text contrast.
layoutSystem.imageCraft: Use believable photography or controlled CGI, natural scale, coherent perspective, grounded contact shadows, tactile texture, subtle imperfection and clear foreground/background separation.

categoryRules.Creative: Create a premium post-ready 4:5 Instagram design with a memorable concept, strong product/type relationship, one to three useful information modules and a coordinated graphic system. It must feel like an agency campaign asset—not a cinematic render, plain poster or basic template.
categoryRules.Flyer: Create an art-directed social flyer with dynamic reading order, strong type scale, grouped information, expressive but controlled shapes and campaign-level finishing.
categoryRules.3D: Use one clear CGI mechanism inside a fully designed social composition. Combine it with real typography, graphic architecture, compact facts and believable depth; never deliver the raw render alone.
categoryRules.Packaging: Use practical shelf hierarchy plus a premium launch-design system: expressive typography, controlled material detail, callouts and campaign framing without changing protected facts.
categoryRules.Video: Use clean but expressive shot design, motivated camera movement, natural timing, strong title cards and coherent motion-graphic modules. Each shot advances the message.

rejectIf: plain product plus headline with no composed design system
generic template layout with weak hierarchy
uncoordinated stickers, badges, blobs, arrows or shapes
generic gradients, neon glow, particles, smoke, splashes or lens effects
centered product on a pedestal without a concept reason
overly glossy, plastic or visibly AI-generated surfaces
perfect template symmetry with no optical adjustment
duplicate product name, claim or CTA
any change to the locked product
qaChecklist: passes the Human-Made Creative Master gate
feels premium and fully designed rather than basic
one to three useful information modules
two to five coordinated graphic devices
human optical spacing and tactile detail
